    )
  );

const backups = H.lane('backups', Backup)
  .handler(backupFlow)
  .suppliers(
    H.clock('backup-clock', Backup, { daily: '01:00' }, (tick) => {
      const night = tick.now.toISOString().slice(0, 10);
      return databases.map((name) => ({ create: { database: name, night }, key: `${name}-${night}` }));
    })
  )
  .store(sqlite.store(Backup, '.harness/ops.db'))
  .retry(noRetry);

const renewals = H.lane('certificate-renewals', CertificateRenewal)
  .handler(renewalFlow)
  .suppliers(
    H.clock('renewal-clock', CertificateRenewal, { weekly: { day: 'sun', at: '03:00' } }, (tick) =>
      domains.map((domain) => ({ create: { domain }, key: `${domain}-${tick.now.toISOString().slice(0, 10)}` }))
    )
  )
  .retry(renewalRetry);

const incidents = H.lane('incidents', Incident)
  .handler(incidentFlow)
  .suppliers(H.operator)
  .store(sqlite.store(Incident, '.harness/ops.db'));

const heartbeatStreak = H.trigger(
  'three-failed-heartbeats',
  H.on.streak(Heartbeat, 'down', 3, (data) => data.service),
  (event, act) =>
    act.create(
      incidents,
      {
        title: `${event.unit.data.service} is down`,
        detail: `Three consecutive heartbeats of ${event.unit.data.service} failed, the last at ${event.at.toISOString()}.`,
      },
      `heartbeat-${event.unit.data.service}`
    )
);

const failedBackup = H.trigger('failed-backup', H.on.enters(Backup, 'failed'), (event, act) =>
  act.create(
    incidents,
    {
      title: `Backup of ${event.unit.data.database} failed`,
      detail: `The ${event.unit.data.night} backup of ${event.unit.data.database} failed and will not retry.`,
    },
    `backup-${event.unit.key}`
  )
);

const slowBackup = H.trigger('slow-backup', H.on.enters(Backup, 'backed-up'), (event, act) => {
  const durationMs = event.attempt?.durationMs ?? 0;
  if (durationMs <= slowBackupMs) return [];
  return act.remember(operationsJournal, {
    text: `When scheduling the ${event.unit.data.database} backup, start it earlier or split it`,
    because: `the ${event.unit.data.night} run took ${Math.round(durationMs / 60_000)} minutes`,
    when: { kinds: [Backup], facets: [database.is(event.unit.data.database)] },
  });
});

const incidentsFirst = H.policy.scheduler('incidents-first', (view) => {
  const incidentWaiting = view.pending.some((unit) => unit.lane === incidents.name);
  const incidentOpen = incidentWaiting || view.active.some((unit) => unit.lane === incidents.name);
  const rank = (unit: PendingView): number =>
    unit.lane === incidents.name ? 0 : unit.lane === heartbeats.name ? 1 : 2;
  const start = view.pending
    .filter((unit) => !(incidentOpen && unit.lane === backups.name))
    .sort((a, b) => rank(a) - rank(b));
  const preempt = incidentWaiting
    ? view.active.filter((unit) => unit.lane !== backups.name && unit.lane !== incidents.name)
    : [];
  return { start, preempt };
});

const control = http.control({
  port: 8080,
  token: H.env('OPS_CONTROL_TOKEN'),
  grants: [H.ops.readWork, H.ops.writeWork, H.ops.resolveHalts, H.ops.readMemory, H.ops.readTelemetry],
});

const incidentPager = slack.notify({

  message: (entry) =>

      : entry.entry === 'halt'
        ? `Incident ${entry.unit ?? ''} needs a human (${entry.halt}, ${entry.status})`
        : `Incident ${entry.unit ?? ''}: ${entry.entry}`,
});

export const operations = H.harness('operations')
  .ledger(sqlite.ledger('.harness/ledger.db'))
  .lanes(incidents, heartbeats, backups, renewals)
  .triggers(heartbeatStreak, failedBackup, slowBackup)
  .scheduler(incidentsFirst)
  .clients(control)
  .observers(incidentPager, markdown.board('BOARD.md'));

import { H } from 'harness-dsl';
import { z } from 'zod';
import * as claudeCode from 'harness-dsl/claude-code';
import * as anthropic from 'harness-dsl/anthropic';
import * as sqlite from 'harness-dsl/sqlite';
import * as jsonl from 'harness-dsl/jsonl';
import * as shell from 'harness-dsl/shell';
import * as ssh from 'harness-dsl/ssh';
import * as markdown from 'harness-dsl/markdown';

const sourceSchema = z.enum(['crm', 'billing', 'inventory', 'web']);
type SourceSystem = z.infer<typeof sourceSchema>;
const sourceSystems: readonly SourceSystem[] = ['crm', 'billing', 'inventory', 'web'];
const sourceFacet = H.facet('source-system', ['crm', 'billing', 'inventory', 'web']);

const NightlyLoad = H.kind('NightlyLoad')
  .data(z.object({ source: sourceSchema, night: z.string(), approvalDeadline: z.string() }))
  .states(
    H.state('scheduled', 'pending'),
    H.state('awaiting-approval', 'active'),
    H.state('loaded', 'terminal', 'success'),
    H.state('loaded-with-warnings', 'terminal', 'success'),
    H.state('rejected', 'terminal', 'failure'),
    H.state('failed', 'terminal', 'failure'),
    H.state('expired', 'terminal', 'neutral')
  )
  .failsTo('failed');

const tasteKind = H.memory('approver-taste', 'taste');
const approverTaste = H.archive('approver-taste-archive', tasteKind, jsonl.memory('memory/taste.jsonl'));
const summaryBriefing = H.briefing('summary-briefing', [approverTaste]);

const sonnet = anthropic.model('claude-sonnet-4-5');
const api = H.pool('api', [{ account: anthropic.account('api', { apiKey: H.env('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY') }), share: 1 }]);

const local = shell.local('local', { slots: 2 });
const etlHost = ssh.host('etl-host', { address: 'etl.internal', user: 'etl', key: H.env('ETL_SSH_KEY'), slots: 2 });

const loadInput = z.object({ source: sourceSchema, night: z.string() });

const extract = H.command('extract')
  .input(loadInput)
  .argv((input) => ['etl', 'extract', '--source', input.source, '--night', input.night])
  .on(etlHost)
  .recovers('rerun');

const validate = H.command('validate')
  .input(loadInput)
  .argv((input) => ['etl', 'validate', '--source', input.source, '--night', input.night])
  .on(local)
  .recovers('rerun');

const load = H.command('load')
  .input(loadInput)
  .argv((input) => ['etl', 'load', '--source', input.source, '--night', input.night])
  .on(etlHost);

const verify = H.command('verify')
  .input(loadInput)
  .output(z.object({ drift: z.enum(['none', 'tolerable', 'intolerable']), report: z.string() }))
  .argv((input) => ['etl', 'verify', '--source', input.source, '--night', input.night, '--json'])
  .on(etlHost)
  .recovers('rerun');

const summarize = H.role('summarize-anomalies')
  .input(z.object({ source: z.string(), night: z.string(), report: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ summary: z.string() }))
  .prompt(
    (input) =>
      `Summarise in plain language the anomalies in the ${input.source} extract for ${input.night}:\n${input.report}`
  )
  .intents(['read']);

const summarizer = H.agent('summarizer', summarize).model(sonnet).recalls(summaryBriefing);

const validationReview = H.halt('validation-review', z.object({ proceed: z.boolean(), note: z.string().optional() }));
const loadApproval = H.halt('load-approval', z.object({ approved: z.boolean(), note: z.string().optional() }));

const backoff = H.policy.retry('exponential-backoff', ({ failures }) =>
  failures > 3 ? 'stop' : { retryInMs: 60_000 * 2 ** (failures - 1) }
);
const noUnitRetry = H.policy.retry('no-unit-retry', () => 'stop');

const nightly = H.flow('nightly-load')
  .for(NightlyLoad)
  .does(async (ctx) => {
    const { source, night } = ctx.unit.data;
    ctx.facet(sourceFacet, source);
    const batch = { source, night };
    const extracted = await ctx.run(extract, batch, { retry: backoff });
    if (!extracted.ok) return ctx.fail(`extract: ${extracted.error}`);
    const validated = await ctx.run(validate, batch);
    const report = validated.ok ? validated.value : validated.error;
    if (!validated.ok) {
      const review = await ctx.halt(validationReview, `Validation failed for ${source} on ${night}:\n\n${report}`);
      if (!review.proceed) return 'rejected';
    }
    const summary = await ctx.run(summarizer, { source, night, report });
    if (!summary.ok) return ctx.fail(`summary: ${summary.error}`);
    await ctx.move('awaiting-approval');
    const approval = await ctx.halt(loadApproval, summary.value.summary);
    if (!approval.approved) return 'rejected';
    const loaded = await ctx.run(load, batch, { retry: backoff });
    if (!loaded.ok) return ctx.fail(`load: ${loaded.error}`);
    const verified = await ctx.run(verify, batch);
    if (!verified.ok) return ctx.fail(`verify: ${verified.error}`);
    if (verified.value.drift === 'none') return 'loaded';
    if (verified.value.drift === 'tolerable') return 'loaded-with-warnings';
    return ctx.fail(`verify found intolerable drift: ${verified.value.report}`);
  });

const nightlyClock = H.clock('nightly-clock', NightlyLoad, { daily: '02:00' }, (tick) => {
  const night = tick.now.toISOString().slice(0, 10);
  const deadline = new Date(tick.now);
  deadline.setUTCHours(9, 0, 0, 0);
  return sourceSystems.map((source) => ({
    create: { source, night, approvalDeadline: deadline.toISOString() },
    key: `${source}-${night}`,
  }));
});

const loads = H.lane('nightly-loads', NightlyLoad)
  .handler(nightly)
  .suppliers(nightlyClock)
  .store(sqlite.store(NightlyLoad, '.harness/loads.db'))
  .retry(noUnitRetry);

const approvalExpires = H.trigger(
  'approval-expires',
  H.on.deadline(NightlyLoad, (data) => new Date(data.approvalDeadline), ['awaiting-approval']),
  (_event, act) => act.move('expired')
);

const fifo = H.policy.scheduler('oldest-first', (view) => ({
  start: [...view.pending].sort((a, b) => b.waitedMs - a.waitedMs),
}));

const approverSession = claudeCode.supervisor({
  grants: [H.ops.readWork, H.ops.resolveHalts, H.ops.readMemory, H.ops.writeMemory, H.ops.readTelemetry],
});

export const dataJob = H.harness('nightly-data-job')
  .ledger(sqlite.ledger('.harness/ledger.db'))
  .lanes(loads)
  .pools(api)
  .triggers(approvalExpires)
  .scheduler(fifo)
  .clients(approverSession)
  .observers(markdown.board('BOARD.md'), markdown.telemetry('TELEMETRY.md'));

import { z } from 'zod';
import { H } from 'harness-dsl';
import type { Metrics, Model, ModelPolicy, Rate, SupplyOf } from 'harness-dsl';
import * as anthropic from 'harness-dsl/anthropic';
import * as claudeCode from 'harness-dsl/claude-code';
import * as http from 'harness-dsl/http';
import * as sqlite from 'harness-dsl/sqlite';
import * as jsonl from 'harness-dsl/jsonl';
import * as shell from 'harness-dsl/shell';
import * as markdown from 'harness-dsl/markdown';

const sectionSchema = z.enum(['news', 'sports', 'opinion']);
const section = H.facet('section', sectionSchema.options);
const reviewerAModel = H.facet('reviewer-a-model');
const reviewerBModel = H.facet('reviewer-b-model');

const submitted = H.state('submitted', 'pending');
const reviewing = H.state('reviewing', 'active');
const returned = H.state('returned', 'waiting');
const accepted = H.state('accepted', 'terminal', 'success');
const withdrawn = H.state('withdrawn', 'terminal', 'neutral');

const draftSchema = z.object({
  title: z.string(),
  body: z.string(),
  section: sectionSchema,
  author: z.string(),
  notes: z.string().optional(),
});
const Draft = H.kind('Draft').data(draftSchema).states(submitted, reviewing, returned, accepted, withdrawn);

const editorTaste = H.memory('editor-taste', 'taste');
const factLessons = H.memory('fact-lessons', 'experience');
const tasteArchive = H.archive('editor-taste', editorTaste, jsonl.memory('content-review/taste.jsonl'));
const lessonArchive = H.archive('fact-lessons', factLessons, jsonl.memory('content-review/fact-lessons.jsonl'));
const reviewerBriefing = H.briefing('reviewer-briefing', [tasteArchive, lessonArchive]);

const editorReview = H.halt(
  'editor-review',
  z.object({ accept: z.boolean(), notes: z.string(), usedA: z.boolean(), usedB: z.boolean() })
);

const reviewer = H.role('reviewer')
  .input(z.object({ title: z.string(), body: z.string(), section: sectionSchema }))
  .output(z.object({ critique: z.string(), claims: z.array(z.string()) }))
  .prompt(draft => `Critique this ${draft.section} draft titled "${draft.title}". List every factual claim.\n\n${draft.body}`);

const incumbentA = anthropic.model('claude-opus-4');
const incumbentB = anthropic.model('claude-sonnet-4');
const challenger = anthropic.model('claude-haiku-4');

function actedOn(metrics: Metrics, model: Model): Rate {
  const asA = metrics.rate({
    among: { ...editorReview.resolved(), facets: [reviewerAModel.is(model.name)] },
    count: { ...editorReview.resolved({ usedA: true }), facets: [reviewerAModel.is(model.name)] },
    days: 90,
  });
  const asB = metrics.rate({
    among: { ...editorReview.resolved(), facets: [reviewerBModel.is(model.name)] },
    count: { ...editorReview.resolved({ usedB: true }), facets: [reviewerBModel.is(model.name)] },
    days: 90,
  });
  const hits = asA.hits + asB.hits;
  const samples = asA.samples + asB.samples;
  return { value: samples === 0 ? null : hits / samples, hits, samples };
}

function reviewerSlot(name: string, mine: Model, rival: Model): ModelPolicy {
  return H.policy.model(name, choice => {
    const own = actedOn(choice.metrics, mine);
    const other = actedOn(choice.metrics, rival);
    const settled = own.samples >= 50 && other.samples >= 50;
    return settled && (own.value ?? 0) < (other.value ?? 0) ? challenger : mine;
  });
}

const reviewerA = H.agent('reviewer-a', reviewer).model(reviewerSlot('reviewer-a-model', incumbentA, incumbentB)).recalls(reviewerBriefing);
const reviewerB = H.agent('reviewer-b', reviewer).model(reviewerSlot('reviewer-b-model', incumbentB, incumbentA)).recalls(reviewerBriefing);

const local = shell.local('local', { slots: 4 });

const mergeCritiques = H.command('merge-critiques')
  .input(z.object({ a: z.string(), b: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ summary: z.string() }))
  .argv(critiques => ['critique-merge', '--a', critiques.a, '--b', critiques.b])
  .on(local)
  .recovers('rerun');

const factCheck = H.command('fact-check')
  .input(z.object({ section: sectionSchema, claims: z.array(z.string()) }))
  .output(z.object({ repeatMistakes: z.array(z.object({ rule: z.string(), because: z.string() })) }))
  .argv(check => ['fact-check', '--section', check.section, ...check.claims])
  .on(local)
  .recovers('rerun');

const reviewFlow = H.flow('review').for(Draft).does(async ctx => {
  const draft = ctx.unit.data;
  ctx.facet(section, draft.section);
  await ctx.move('reviewing');
  const input = { title: draft.title, body: draft.body, section: draft.section };
  const a = await ctx.run(reviewerA, input);
  const b = await ctx.run(reviewerB, input);
  if (!a.ok || !b.ok) return ctx.fail('a reviewer did not produce a critique');
  if (a.model) ctx.facet(reviewerAModel, a.model);
  if (b.model) ctx.facet(reviewerBModel, b.model);
  const checked = await ctx.run(factCheck, { section: draft.section, claims: [...a.value.claims, ...b.value.claims] });
  if (checked.ok) {
    for (const mistake of checked.value.repeatMistakes) {
      await ctx.remember(lessonArchive, { text: mistake.rule, because: mistake.because, when: { roles: [reviewer] } });
    }
  }
  const merged = await ctx.run(mergeCritiques, { a: a.value.critique, b: b.value.critique });
  if (!merged.ok) return ctx.fail(merged.error);
  const verdict = await ctx.halt(editorReview, merged.value.summary);
  if (verdict.accept) return 'accepted';
  await ctx.update({ notes: verdict.notes });
  return 'returned';
});

const cmsBody = z.object({
  drafts: z.array(
    z.object({
      id: z.string(),
      title: z.string(),
      body: z.string(),
      section: sectionSchema,
      author: z.string(),
      status: z.enum(['submitted', 'resubmitted', 'withdrawn']),
    })
  ),
});

function readCms(body: z.infer<typeof cmsBody>): SupplyOf<typeof Draft>[] {
  const supply: SupplyOf<typeof Draft>[] = [];
  for (const d of body.drafts) {
    if (d.status === 'withdrawn') supply.push({ update: d.id, state: 'withdrawn' });
    else if (d.status === 'resubmitted') supply.push({ update: d.id, patch: { title: d.title, body: d.body }, state: 'submitted' });
    else supply.push({ create: { title: d.title, body: d.body, section: d.section, author: d.author }, key: d.id });
  }
  return supply;
}

const cmsHeaders = { authorization: H.env('CMS_TOKEN') };

const draftLane = H.lane('drafts', Draft)
  .handler(reviewFlow)
  .suppliers(http.poll(Draft, { url: 'https://cms.example.com/api/drafts', every: { minutes: 10 }, headers: cmsHeaders, body: cmsBody, read: readCms }))
  .store(http.store(Draft, { url: 'https://cms.example.com/api/drafts', headers: cmsHeaders, stateField: 'review_state' }))
  .wip(3);

const returnedNotesBecomeTaste = H.trigger('returned-notes-become-taste', H.on.enters(Draft, 'returned'), (event, act) => {
  const notes = event.unit.data.notes;
  if (!notes) return [];
  return act.remember(tasteArchive, {
    text: `When reviewing ${event.unit.data.section} drafts, ${notes}`,
    because: `the editor returned "${event.unit.data.title}" with this note`,
    status: 'candidate',
    when: { kinds: [Draft], roles: [reviewer], facets: [section.is(event.unit.data.section)] },
  });
});

const apiPool = H.pool('api', [{ account: anthropic.account('publication-api', { apiKey: H.env('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY') }), share: 1 }]);

const oldestFirst = H.policy.scheduler('oldest-first', view => ({
  start: [...view.pending].sort((x, y) => y.waitedMs - x.waitedMs),
}));

export const contentReview = H.harness('content-review')
  .ledger(sqlite.ledger('content-review/ledger.db'))
  .lanes(draftLane)
  .pools(apiPool)
  .triggers(returnedNotesBecomeTaste)
  .scheduler(oldestFirst)

import { z } from 'zod';
import { H } from 'harness-dsl';

import * as markdown from 'harness-dsl/markdown';

const HOUR_MS = 3_600_000;
const TWO_WEEKS_MS = 14 * 24 * HOUR_MS;
const local = shell.local('local', { slots: 4 });
const store = 'lifecycles/units.db';

const proposed = H.state('proposed', 'pending');
const measuring = H.state('measuring', 'pending');
const running = H.state('running', 'waiting');
const aWins = H.state('a-wins', 'terminal', 'success');
const bWins = H.state('b-wins', 'terminal', 'success');
const inconclusive = H.state('inconclusive', 'terminal', 'neutral');

const Experiment = H.kind('Experiment')
  .data(z.object({ hypothesis: z.string(), startedAt: z.string().optional(), a: z.array(z.number()), b: z.array(z.number()) }))
  .states(proposed, measuring, running, aWins, bWins, inconclusive);

const measure = H.command('measure-experiment')
  .input(z.object({ experiment: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ a: z.number(), b: z.number() }))
  .argv(target => ['experiment-metric', target.experiment])
  .on(local)
  .recovers('rerun');

type ExperimentVerdict = 'a-wins' | 'b-wins' | 'inconclusive';
function average(values: readonly number[]): number {
  return values.length === 0 ? 0 : values.reduce((sum, v) => sum + v, 0) / values.length;
}
const experimentVerdict = H.policy.rule(
  'experiment-verdict',
  (samples: { readonly a: readonly number[]; readonly b: readonly number[] }): ExperimentVerdict => {
    const lift = average(samples.b) - average(samples.a);
    const margin = Math.max(Math.abs(average(samples.a)), 1) * 0.02;
    if (lift > margin) return 'b-wins';
    if (lift < -margin) return 'a-wins';
    return 'inconclusive';
  }
);

const experimentFlow = H.flow('experiment').for(Experiment).does(async ctx => {
  const now = ctx.now();
  const started = ctx.unit.data.startedAt ? new Date(ctx.unit.data.startedAt) : now;
  const reading = await ctx.run(measure, { experiment: ctx.unit.key });
  if (!reading.ok) return ctx.fail(reading.error);
  const a = [...ctx.unit.data.a, reading.value.a];
  const b = [...ctx.unit.data.b, reading.value.b];
  await ctx.update({ startedAt: started.toISOString(), a, b });
  if (now.getTime() - started.getTime() >= TWO_WEEKS_MS) return await ctx.decide(experimentVerdict, { a, b });
  return ctx.wait('running', { at: new Date(now.getTime() + HOUR_MS), then: 'measuring' });
});

  .input(z.object({ release: z.string(), platform: platformSchema }))
  .argv(s => ['smoke', '--release', s.release, '--platform', s.platform])
  .on(local)
  .recovers('rerun');

  .input(z.object({ version: z.string(), buildLog: z.string() }))

    if (!built.ok) return ctx.fail(built.error);
    const announced = await ctx.run(announce, { version: release.version, channel: release.channel });
    if (!announced.ok) return ctx.fail(announced.error);
    const reviewed = await ctx.run(reviewer, { version: release.version, buildLog: built.value.log });
    if (!reviewed.ok) return ctx.fail(reviewed.error);
    const approval = await ctx.halt(releaseApproval, `${release.version}: reviewer says ${reviewed.value.verdict}\n${reviewed.value.notes}`);

# You are designing harness-dsl, a TypeScript DSL for stateful agentic-work harnesses.

# harness-dsl design principles

These are the owner's decisions. A variant that violates one is worse, however elegant. A variant may propose changing one only by stating the principle it breaks and why, in its design notes.

## Vision

1. **Stateless LLMs, stateful harness.** Every model call is a pure function. All state lives in the harness. The harness gets better over time not because models learn but because it feeds the right memory to the right call.
2. **The harness is about work.** Units of work, kinds of work (Bug, Feature, Epic, ServiceHeartbeat, Exercise), hierarchies of kinds, lifecycles, where work comes from, where its state lives, what runs next. The framework is honest about this. It does not hide behind "general purpose".
3. **An LLM is a component, not a requirement.** A harness with zero model calls is a first-class harness. Deterministic scripts and model calls compose through the same executable interface.
4. **Intelligence lives in determinism.** Policies (what to pick, what to recall, what to schedule) are deterministic functions, authored once, reading harness state and metrics at decision time. Policies never change themselves. The harness changes behaviour because policies read changed state.

## Dividing line

5. **Opinionated about shape, agnostic about backend.** The kernel defines what a work unit, a lifecycle, a memory item, a policy, a ledger entry *is*. It never cares where any of them is stored, which vendor serves a model, or which tool the operator uses. Like Eloquent: strict about how you model, indifferent to which database.
6. **Defaults ship, and pass the delete test.** First-party backends ship in the box (SQLite ledger, JSONL memory store, Claude Code driver, folder supplier). Each is one implementation of a public interface. Delete any of them and the kernel still compiles and runs.
7. **`H.*` is kernel vocabulary only.** Shapes and builders. Anything with a backend lives in a subpath (`harness-dsl/claude-code`, `harness-dsl/sqlite`, `harness-dsl/linear`), whether first-party or not. No vendor, CLI, file format or product name appears in `H.*`.
8. **Three sorts of entity.** *Kinds* are pure vocabulary and carry no backend (work kind, state, memory kind, role). *Instances* are specific resources and carry their backend (account, model, runner). *Pivots* connect kinds and instances per harness (pool = accounts × policy, agent = role × model, lane = work kind × suppliers × store × handler, journal = memory kind × store × recall).
9. **Every pivot has a noun.** A pivot enters the DSL only when we can name what it produces. `bind`, `wire`, `attach`, `connect` are not nouns; they are the absence of a concept.
10. **Relationships do not live on kinds.** A work kind does not know who supplies it, stores it or handles it. A role does not know which model runs it. Putting a relationship on a kind makes the kind less reusable.

## Mechanics

11. **Descriptors are immutable and stateless.** Every builder method returns a new descriptor. Nothing is read from the environment at definition time; `H.env('NAME')` and `H.slot.port(n)` are references the runtime resolves. Derived descriptors must be renamed; the runtime refuses two descriptors with one name.
12. **Lifecycle skeleton.** An attempt has one of three outcomes: succeeded, failed, cancelled. This is the harness's track record, and metrics on models, agents, runners and accounts are computed from it. A unit is at one of four positions: pending, active, waiting (parked, holding no capacity, not schedulable), terminal. The scheduler and the board are defined on positions. A kind's named states are entities (shareable); each declares its position, and each terminal state declares its verdict for the kind's own outcome rate: success, failure or neutral, with no default. Blocked (waiting on a human) is an attempt state, not a unit state. A unit outlives its attempts. By default a failed attempt leaves the unit at pending under the lane's retry policy; a kind may declare a move for a failure, and only then does an attempt's failure move the unit. (Amended 2026-11-01 after generation 0: eight of eight variants broke the five-outcome form, and the adversaries showed why. The failure default was added after generation 1, when three of eleven children read the silence as "every kind declares a failure state" and invented states that loop or dead-end.)
13. **Triggers are relationships.** A trigger connects a source (a transition, later also time, external events, metric thresholds) to a consequence (create work in a lane, run an executable, record memory). Flows stay blind to other kinds. Triggers fire only from recorded ledger events and their firings are recorded.
14. **Memory is forward-phrased and atomic.** "Do X when Y because Z", never history. The kernel owns the envelope (id, created, `when`: the kinds, roles, skills and resources an item applies to). Recall is a deterministic policy over items and scope, ranked by specificity and by track record (items present in succeeded attempts rise). Experience (can be wrong, stale, deduped) and taste (the owner's preference, never wrong, broadly scoped) are different kinds.
15. **The ledger is the kernel's only state.** Runs, attempts, invocations, transitions, the pending queue, quota. Its backend is pluggable, and it may be partitioned by backend. Account quota shared by several harnesses is a ledger partition of append-only quota events: each harness appends its own consumption and folds the window at read time, so no harness takes a lock over another's account state. A quota store that needs the ledger's single-writer lock, or a second store under the ledger's name, breaks this principle. There is no kernel work store: domain state lives where the owner's adapter puts it, and a unit may have no store at all. (Shared quota ruled 2026-11-01 after generation 1.)
16. **Supply, store and scheduling are three pillars.** Suppliers produce units (folder, poll, webhook, schedule, operator). Stores hold unit state (one adapter may be both). The scheduler decides what runs next from pending units, lane WIP limits, capacity (runner slots, account eligibility) and a policy. Without a scheduler there is a library, not a harness.
17. **Human-in-the-loop is kernel.** Halting an attempt for an outside decision is universal. Who resolves it, through which surface, is not: the supervisor is one optional client of a control API made of operations, and operations (not capability strings) are what a client is granted.
18. **Metrics are queryable and honest.** Computed from ledger transitions, with sample counts beside every rate, so policy authors write exploration deliberately. Success is defined by the kind's terminal states, never by "the flow finished".

## Ergonomics standards

19. A first-time reader predicts what each line does from its name. Builders chain. Names are nouns for things and verbs for settings. Units sit in names or types (`budgetTokens`, `maxUsd`), never implied.
20. Full inference. Scenario code needs no `as`, `any`, `!` or `@ts-ignore`. A `.d.ts` that uses `any` to make inference "work" fails this standard.
21. Small surface. The fewest entities and methods that express the whole scenario battery without escape hatches. An entity with one use is suspect. A method nobody in the battery calls is removed.
22. No two words for one thing. Run, attempt, invocation, step have one definition each, or fewer words.


# Scenario battery

# Scenario 1: coding team

A product team's harness, the shape harness-dsl was first built for.

## Must express

- Three kinds of work in a hierarchy: Epic decomposes into Features; Bugs arrive on their own. Epic completes when its Features do. Feature and Bug share most of their lifecycle and handler but differ in how many build-and-audit rounds they get (Bug 3, Feature 5).
- Supply from three places at once for Bugs: an issue tracker (Linear), a folder of markdown files, and the operator typing to the supervisor. Features from the tracker and the operator. Epics from the tracker only.
- Bug and Feature state is kept in the tracker; the harness is not the source of truth for them.
- A builder agent on a worktree per attempt, with a file-lease guard (two attempts may not write the same file) and a stop check that runs the project's checks before the agent may stop.
- An auditor agent that finds deficits; the loop continues until none remain or rounds run out. The builder may halt the attempt for an owner decision.
- Accounts: three Claude subscriptions in a pool with per-account quota shares, drained soonest-expiring first, falling back to an API account. Model choice for the builder reads the ledger: use the cheaper model until its success rate on this kind of work, over 14 days and at least 20 samples, drops below 0.85.
- Memory: experience ("when touching payments, run the ledger fixture first, because the migration reorders rows") recalled by builder and auditor, recorded by the auditor; taste ("prefer early returns over nested conditionals") recalled by builder and planner, written by the owner.
- A service heartbeat every five minutes, all deterministic, whose failure creates a Bug through a trigger. The heartbeat flow must not reference the Bug kind.
- Scheduler: heartbeats first, then bugs, features, epics; a WIP limit of 2 concurrent bugs and 1 epic; starvation protection for features.
- Supervisor: a Claude Code session granted read and write on work, blocker resolution, memory writes, telemetry and account shares, plus one custom operation (a production health probe).
- Board and telemetry projections written as Markdown files.

## Hostile aspects

- The heartbeat kind must have no store and must still appear in telemetry.
- The same handler flow serves two kinds with different round counts without duplication.
- The model-choice policy must expose sample counts; a variant that hides them fails.


---

# Scenario 2: support triage

Customer conversations arrive from a helpdesk webhook. Nothing here touches files.

## Must express

- One kind of work, Conversation, supplied by a webhook (push) and by a periodic poll of the helpdesk for anything the webhook missed. State lives in the helpdesk via its API; the harness holds nothing but its ledger.
- Lifecycle: new, classifying, drafting, awaiting approval, sent, closed by customer, escalated. A human approves every outgoing reply (halt), except for a category the policy marks safe after 200 approved samples with zero rejections.
- Two agents: a classifier on a cheap model, a drafter on a stronger one. The drafter recalls taste (tone, phrases to avoid) and experience ("when the customer mentions a refund older than 30 days, cite policy 4.2"). A reviewer role (human, through the supervisor) records taste from its edits.
- Deadlines: each conversation carries an SLA; the scheduler orders by time to breach, not by arrival. A breached SLA fires a trigger that escalates (creates an Escalation unit in another lane with its own handler and a human-only flow).
- External cancellation: if the customer replies while a draft is awaiting approval, the attempt is cancelled and the unit returns to classifying with the new message.
- Per-unit cost ceiling: no conversation may spend more than $0.40 of model cost; a unit that would exceed it halts for a human.
- Metrics the policy reads: approval rate by category and by model, with sample counts.

## Hostile aspects

- Cancellation from outside an active attempt.
- A trigger whose source is time (SLA breach), not a transition.
- A cost ceiling scoped to a unit, not an account.
- A lane whose handler contains no model call at all (Escalation).


---

# Scenario 3: research pipeline

A team runs literature-style research: a topic goes in, a sourced report comes out.

## Must express

- Kind Topic, supplied by the operator and by a weekly schedule that re-opens topics tagged "recurring". Topics are stored in the harness's own store (no external system), so the first-party store is the right choice here.
- Handler: fan out 20 search-and-extract calls as one cloud batch on a cheap model (the batch API discount matters), gather, then one synthesis call on a strong model, then a deterministic citation check command that fails the attempt if a citation does not resolve.
- Memory with a vector-store backend: prior report findings are a memory kind recalled by the synthesizer by semantic similarity. Recall is still a deterministic policy; the vector store is a backend. Experience about sources ("when the source is a preprint server, downgrade confidence") is a second kind in a JSONL store.
- Per-topic cost ceiling of $3; the scheduler never starts a topic whose projected cost (from the metric: mean cost of succeeded attempts of this kind) would pass the remaining daily budget of $40.
- Outcome: a report is delivered, or the topic is parked (not enough sources), or it is cancelled by the operator. Parked is not failure.
- The synthesizer's model is chosen by a policy that compares two strong models on a metric the owner defines: citation-check pass rate.

## Hostile aspects

- A memory backend that is not a file and a recall policy that uses similarity, while recall stays deterministic.
- A cloud batch step inside a flow, priced at the batch discount in telemetry.
- Budget as a scheduling input (daily, across units).
- A terminal outcome, parked, that is neither success nor failure.


---

# Scenario 4: operations, no model anywhere

A platform team uses the harness purely as a durable scheduler of deterministic work. There is no model, no account, no agent in this harness. If a variant needs any of them to compile or start, it fails the scenario.

## Must express

- Kinds: Heartbeat (every 5 minutes per service), Backup (nightly per database), CertificateRenewal (weekly check, act when under 14 days), Incident (created by triggers, handled by a runbook flow that pages a human and waits).
- Suppliers: schedules only, plus the operator creating Incidents by hand through the control API over plain HTTP (no Claude Code, no MCP).
- Runners: local for heartbeats; SSH to two hosts for backups and renewals, with per-host concurrency of 1 and a disk-space preflight.
- Triggers: three consecutive failed heartbeats of one service create an Incident (a trigger over a pattern of transitions, not a single transition). A failed Backup creates an Incident at once. A Backup that succeeded but took over 2 hours records a note in a journal of operational experience, which is also a memory kind, even though nothing here reads memory into a prompt; the supervisor reads it.
- The Incident flow halts for a human acknowledgement, then runs a runbook command, then halts for a human to confirm resolution.
- Scheduler: Incidents preempt everything; a running Backup is not interrupted, but no new Backup starts while an Incident is active.
- Observers: a Slack notification on every Incident transition, and the board file.

## Hostile aspects

- Zero model calls: every executable is a command.
- A trigger whose source is a pattern across several transitions.
- Preemption rules in the scheduler.
- A control API client that is plain HTTP.
- A memory kind with no agent reading it.


---

# Scenario 5: data job with approval

A nightly data job with one human gate in the middle and a retry policy.

## Must express

- Kind NightlyLoad, supplied by a schedule at 02:00, one unit per source system (four). State in the harness's store.
- Handler: extract (command, SSH runner), validate (command), then a model call that writes a plain-language summary of anomalies, then halt for a human to approve the load, then load (command), then verify (command).
- Retry: extract and load retry up to 3 times with exponential backoff on failure, as a policy on the step, not hand-written in the command. A validation failure does not retry; it halts for a human with the validation report.
- Outcome: loaded, loaded with warnings (verify found tolerable drift), rejected by the approver, or failed. Loaded with warnings is a success for scheduling purposes but must be distinguishable in metrics and on the board.
- A unit left waiting for approval past 09:00 is cancelled by a time trigger and a new one is not created until the next night.
- Resumability: if the harness process restarts while a unit is blocked on approval, the unit is still blocked after restart and resumes at the same step when approved.
- The approver works through the supervisor; the summary agent recalls taste about what the approver wants emphasised.

## Hostile aspects

- Retry with backoff as a declared policy on a step.
- Restart survival of a blocked attempt.
- A success-with-warnings outcome that is success to the scheduler and distinct to metrics.
- A time trigger that cancels, scoped to one kind.


---

# Scenario 6: content review driven by taste

A publication runs drafts through review. The point of this harness is that it learns the owner's taste.

## Must express

- Kind Draft, supplied from a CMS by poll, state in the CMS.
- Handler: two reviewer agents on two different models each produce a critique; a deterministic command merges them; the editor (human, supervisor) accepts or returns the draft with notes.
- Taste memory grows from the editor's notes: every returned draft's notes become candidate taste items through a trigger (returned → record taste candidate), curated by the editor later through the control API (accept, merge, drop). Reviewers recall taste; taste applies to all drafts, with a smaller set scoped to a section (`sports`, `opinion`).
- A/B on models: the two reviewers' models are chosen by a policy that reads which reviewer's critiques the editor acted on more (a metric the owner defines from editor actions recorded as transitions), with sample counts, and swaps the weaker model after 50 samples.
- Experience memory also exists (fact-checking lessons), recalled by both reviewers, recorded by the fact-check command when it finds a repeat mistake.
- No worktrees, no files, no code.

## Hostile aspects

- Memory capture as a trigger consequence, not an agent tool.
- Curation operations on memory (merge, drop) exposed to the supervisor.
- A metric defined by the owner from recorded operator actions, not from attempt outcomes.
- Two agents of the same role on different models in one flow.


---

# Scenario 7: two projects, shared subscriptions

The owner runs two independent product harnesses (two repositories, two ledgers, two supervisors) that share the same three Claude subscription accounts.

## Must express

- Each harness declares the same three accounts. Account quota state (utilization windows, cooldowns) is shared between the two harnesses: if harness A drives an account into cooldown, harness B sees it. Project share caps are per harness: A may use 60% of an account's window, B 30%.
- Each harness has its own ledger (runs, attempts, telemetry) in its own SQLite file. Neither can see the other's runs.
- Fair scheduling across tenants is not the kernel's job (they are separate processes), but each scheduler must respect account eligibility that the other may have changed a second ago.
- Harness A is the coding team of scenario 1. Harness B is a documentation harness: kind DocPage, supplied from a folder, handled by a writer agent and a link-check command, stored in the folder's frontmatter.
- A shared taste journal: both harnesses recall the owner's taste from one JSONL file; each has its own experience journal.
- The owner's one supervisor session can be pointed at either harness (two control API endpoints) and sees the shared account state from both.

## Hostile aspects

- Account state that outlives and spans harnesses: where does it live, and is that a second kernel store or a backend of the ledger?
- Two ledgers, one memory store, three shared accounts: the design must say which entity owns which state without new ad-hoc concepts.
- The same entity definitions (accounts, taste journal) imported by two harness files from a shared module.


---

# Scenario 8: lifecycles that do not fit

Three kinds of work chosen to break a pending/active/succeeded/failed/cancelled skeleton. A variant must express them without lying: mapping an outcome onto a skeleton state it does not mean is a failure of this scenario.

## Must express

- **Experiment**: an A/B test unit runs for two weeks, collecting a metric from a command every hour. It ends in one of: A wins, B wins, inconclusive. None of these is failure. The scheduler must treat all three as terminal; metrics must distinguish them; a policy elsewhere must be able to ask "how often are experiments inconclusive?"
- **Tenancy**: a customer's tenancy is a unit of work that is never terminal while the customer is a customer. It is re-evaluated monthly (usage review, a model-written summary, a human decision to upsell or not) and may be suspended and reinstated any number of times. It ends only on churn, which is neither success nor failure. The scheduler must not consider an active tenancy as occupying capacity between evaluations.
- **Negotiation**: a procurement negotiation unit alternates between the harness (an agent drafts the next offer) and the outside world (the vendor replies, via a webhook supplier that updates an existing unit rather than creating one). It may end in agreement, walk-away by us (a decision, not a failure), walk-away by them, or expiry (a time trigger). Each attempt is one round; the unit outlives many attempts.

## Hostile aspects

- Terminal states that are neither success nor failure, needed by metrics.
- A unit that is active for years and must not hold capacity.
- A supplier that updates an existing unit instead of creating one.
- An attempt-per-round model where the unit's identity spans attempts and external replies.
- If the variant changes the skeleton (adds outcomes, replaces the five with something else), its design notes must say what success rate means afterwards.


---

# Scenario 9: a harness watching itself

The support harness of scenario 2 observes its own metrics and acts on them. Nothing here is new work from outside; every unit created here is created by the harness about itself.

## Must express

- A trigger whose source is a metric threshold: when the approval rate for a category over the last 7 days falls below 0.9 with at least 50 samples, the harness creates one Audit unit for that category in an `audits` lane with a human-only handler. While an Audit for that category is open, no second one is created, however many samples cross the threshold.
- The same crossing records a candidate experience item scoped to the drafter role and the category: "when drafting for {category}, recall the stricter phrasing, because approvals fell to {rate}".
- When the category's rate recovers above 0.95, the open Audit is cancelled. Below 0.9 and above 0.95 are two thresholds on purpose: the trigger fires on a crossing, once, not on every sample.
- A trigger that pauses the `conversations` lane when the harness's own model error rate over the last hour exceeds 0.2 with at least 20 invocations, and resumes it when the rate falls below 0.05. Paused means: nothing new starts in the lane, running attempts finish. Both the pause and the resume are recorded on the ledger and visible on the board, with the metric value that caused them.
- Each conversation's SLA can be extended by the reviewer through the supervisor. The breach timer moves with the new deadline; the old deadline never fires.
- A policy elsewhere must be able to ask "how many Audits were opened per category this month" and "how long was the lane paused in total".

## Hostile aspects

- A trigger source that is a metric, not a transition, a time or an external event; it still fires only from recorded ledger state and its firings are recorded.
- Hysteresis: two thresholds, one firing per crossing.
- Deduplication by a group key (the category), not by kind.
- A consequence that acts on a lane, not on a unit, and is itself a recorded, queryable fact.
- A timer whose deadline changes after it was armed.


---

# Scenario 10: the power goes off

A release harness is killed mid-attempt (power cut, OOM, `kill -9`, laptop closed) and started again. This scenario states what must be true after the restart. It does not say how; a variant that satisfies every line by any mechanism passes, and its design.md must name the mechanism and what the harness author had to write for it.

## Must express

- Kind Release, supplied by the operator. Its flow, in order: `build` (a command that is safe to run twice), `announce` (a command that posts a message to a channel; posting twice is wrong), `review` (an agent on a model), `approval` (a halt for a release manager), `summarize` (a model call submitted to a batch API and collected later), then it spawns one Smoke unit per platform in a `smoke` lane and waits for them.
- After a restart, a step that completed before the crash is not run again and costs nothing.
- The step that was running at the crash is handled per step, declared by the harness author on the step or the command: rerun it (`build`), never rerun it and park the attempt for the supervisor (`announce`, unless the harness can tell that the post happened, in which case it continues), or ask the step's driver whether it finished (`review`: the agent's session may have completed while the harness was down).
- An `approval` halt resolved while the harness was down is found on restart and the flow continues from it.
- A `summarize` batch submitted before the crash is collected, not resubmitted.
- A resumed attempt is the same attempt: one id, one row in every metric, and the crash is never counted as a model failure or an agent failure.
- Smoke children that finished while the parent was down are seen by the parent on restart; children still running are not restarted.
- An attempt whose flow definition changed between the crash and the restart (a step renamed, a step inserted before the one that was running) is not silently rerun. It is parked for the supervisor with a reason, and the supervisor can restart it from the top or abandon it.
- The harness author writes no resumption code: no checkpoint, no "if already done" branch in a flow, no reading of the ledger from a flow.
- Two copies of the harness started against the same ledger by mistake: the second refuses to start, or takes over from a dead first, and never both run.

## Hostile aspects

- Effects of three kinds (safe to repeat, wrong to repeat, outside the harness's control) in one flow, each with its own restart behaviour, declared by the author and enforced by the kernel.
- State that moved while the harness was down (a halt resolved, a batch completed, a child finished) and must be found, not replayed from memory.
- A definition that changed under a running attempt.
- Single-writer exclusion over a shared ledger.
- Everything above must hold with the ledger as the only kernel state (principle 15), and the author must have nothing to write for it (principle 2).


# Judging rubric

Judges compare two variants, A and B, and name a winner on one criterion. Never score in isolation. Never reward length or completeness of prose. Prefer the variant a stranger could use correctly after reading its scenario files once.

## Criteria (one comparison per criterion)

- **fidelity**: which variant violates fewer principles in `principles.md`, and violates none of 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11? Each violation is a strike; a strike on a dividing-line principle counts double.
- **ergonomics**: in the scenario files, which variant lets a reader predict each line's effect from its name, keeps builder chains consistent, and needs fewer things explained?
- **expressiveness**: across the battery, which variant expresses the scenarios with fewer workarounds, fewer raw strings standing in for entities, and no lies (mapping an outcome onto a skeleton state it does not mean)?
- **economy**: which variant achieves the same coverage with a smaller surface: fewer entities, fewer methods, no one-use entity, no unused method?
- **connectedness**: which variant's entities connect through named pivots, with no orphan concept, no hidden coupling (a flow that secretly knows another kind, a role that knows a vendor), and no two words for one thing?

## Framings (each comparison is asked under one framing)

- **laravel**: you maintain a framework loved for striking the line between what it decides and what it leaves open. Judge whether the variant decides the right things.
- **durable**: you build durable-execution engines (Temporal, Step Functions). Judge whether the execution model (attempts, re-entry, cancellation, blocked, spawn) will survive contact with real failures.
- **newcomer**: you have never seen harness-dsl. You must implement the scenario named in the prompt tonight. Judge which variant you would rather be handed.
- **owner**: judge strictly against `principles.md`, nothing else.
- **adversary**: for each variant, find the scenario in the battery it handles worst, and judge which variant's worst case is less bad.

## Output

Return exactly one JSON object and nothing else:

{"winner": "A" | "B", "confidence": 0.5-1.0, "reasons": ["...", "..."]}

Reasons are specific: quote the line or name that decided it. At most three.


# Known weaknesses of the owner's own seed

# Known weaknesses of the seed design (as of 2026-11-01)

These are the gaps I can see without the loop. They are fed to the adversary as "known; find what we did not see", and to mutation as targets.

1. **Flows are coupled to state entities.** `ticketFlow` names `Working`, `Done`, `Abandoned`, so any kind handled by it must own those states. Shared state entities soften this; they do not remove it. Alternative not explored: flows transition to skeleton outcomes and the lane maps them to the kind's states.
2. **`spawn` with `await: true` holds a slot** while children run. The better engine behaviour is that the attempt ends at the spawn and the kind's flow re-enters when children terminate, so an Epic has several attempts. Not designed.
3. **Roles name Claude Code tools** (`.tools(['Read', 'Edit'])`). A role is vocabulary; tool names are a driver's. Should be intents the driver maps.
4. **`.resources()` is path-shaped.** Resources might be entities (`H.resource`) so leases and memory scope can name services, databases, environments, not only globs.
5. **Triggers only fire on transitions.** Time (an SLA breach, a deadline), external events (a customer replied, a PR was merged) and metric thresholds are also sources. Not designed.
6. **Cancellation of active work from outside** (an external event cancels a unit mid-attempt) is not designed. Neither is preemption by the scheduler.
7. **Deadlines, SLAs and per-unit cost ceilings** are not inputs anywhere. Quota is per account; nothing caps what one unit may spend.
8. **Shared accounts across harnesses.** Account quota state lives in each harness's ledger, so two projects sharing a subscription double-count. Account state may need its own shareable backend, separate from the ledger.
9. **The learning loop has no capture entity.** `.record()` lets an agent write, and the supervisor can write; nothing turns outcomes into candidate memories automatically (a failed attempt proposing an experience item). Triggers to journals would do it; the connection is not drawn.
10. **Execution vocabulary is loose.** Run, attempt, invocation, step: four words for levels of execution, used without definitions. The ledger needs them defined.
11. **A handler flow's `.input()` duplicates the lane's kind.** `H.flow.for(Bug)` or the lane supplying the input type would remove the repetition and the chance of mismatch.
12. **Journal reads union across journals of a kind, writes need one destination.** Justified, but asymmetric and unstated in the DSL.
13. **Perpetual units.** A long-lived unit (a running service, a tenancy) that is never terminal does not fit a skeleton of pending/active/terminal. Multi-outcome units (an experiment ending in A, B or inconclusive) fit badly: mapping inconclusive to failed is a lie.
14. **Observers are the one non-entity.** Board and telemetry are functions; alerting (Slack on failure) and webhooks would be more of the same. Possibly fine as "subscriber" shape; possibly a missing noun.
15. **The supervisor's client hides its transport.** A dashboard client would need HTTP, not MCP. Maybe fine; maybe transport is a separate thing.
16. **Startup validation is implicit.** Name collisions (derived descriptors keep their name), transitions outside the kind's states, a trigger on a lane that is not registered: all should fail at `start()`, none is specified.
17. **Journal is the weakest noun in the set.** Curated items are not a journal.

# Variant g03-durable--1-2-1-0

Mechanical scores: compile errors 0, escapes 0, any-in-dts 0, surface 256, coverage 10/10, cannot: none, strikes: none

=== FILE: design.md ===
# harness-dsl: units as processes, memory as playbooks (child of g02-durable-le-1-2-1)

The lens is still Erlang/OTP. A unit is a `gen_statem`, its received events are its mailbox, timers are statem timeouts, and `spawn` monitors children. This generation does three things:

- It renames the weakest noun: **journal → playbook**.
- It repairs the parent's three named defects: shadow statuses, flows coupled to state names, and silently dropped events.
- It fixes the worst-scenario defects: halts holding lane capacity, and unbounded rejection loops.

## The rename: journal → playbook

The pivot is memory kind × memory store × recall policy. A *journal* is a diary of what happened, and principle 14 forbids exactly that: memory is forward-phrased ("do X when Y because Z"), never history. Known weakness 17 already said so ("curated items are not a journal").

What the pivot produces is a body of forward rules that an agent consults before acting and that grows from outcomes. That is a **playbook**: a set of plays, each with a situation it applies to (`when`) and a reason (`because`). The noun also fits both memory sorts:

- An experience playbook can hold a stale play.
- A taste playbook is the owner's house style.
- Curation (accept, merge, drop) is how anyone maintains a playbook.

What changes with the rename:

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `H.journal(name, kind)` | `H.playbook(name, kind)` |
| `Journal` | `Playbook` (`.store`, `.recall`) |
| `JournalSpec` | `PlaybookSpec` |
| — | `MemoryItem.playbook` (new) |

Agents call `.recalls(playbooks)` and `.records(playbook)`. Triggers call `.records(playbook, make)`. The verb "records" stays: recording a play into a playbook reads correctly.

The read/write asymmetry (known weakness 12) is stated as follows:
- An agent recalls from several playbooks.
- An agent records into exactly one.
- A playbook is one store, so a write has one destination.

## Execution vocabulary (one definition each)

**Unit.** One piece of work of one kind in one lane, identified by `(lane, key)`.
- Keys are unique forever. A create with an existing key records `unit.deduplicated`.
- A unit outlives its attempts.
- Its **position is always its state's declared position.** There is no flag beside it.

**Attempt.** One pass of the lane's flow over a unit.
- Its status while open is `running` or `blocked`.
- Its outcome is `succeeded`, `failed` or `cancelled`.
- **Blocked** means waiting on a human. The reasons are `decision`, `question`, `budget`, `failure`, `restart` and `definition`.

**Halt.** The flow step that blocks an attempt. Halt is the verb; blocked is the status.

**Step.** One named node of a flow.

**Invocation.** One execution of an executable in a step. A retry is a new invocation.

**Removed words:**
- *parked* (the `UnitView.parked` flag);
- *receiving* (`AttemptView.receiving`, `ReceiveView`);
- *mark*;
- `event.ignored`;
- `unit.parked`;
- `unit.requeued`.

"Not progressing" is now said in exactly two places:
- a unit's position (`waiting`);
- an attempt's status (`blocked`).

## Capacity: who holds what

This rule repairs the worst scenario (2) and the adversary's contract-counsel scenario.

| Resource | Held by | Released when |
|---|---|---|
| Lane WIP | a **running** attempt | the attempt blocks or ends |
| Runner slot | an attempt **during an invocation** | the invocation ends; `Runner.reacquire(attemptId)` restores the same workdir (worktree) |
| Account quota | an invocation | the invocation ends |

Consequences:
- A blocked attempt holds no WIP, no slot and no account. Ten conversations awaiting approval, or forty contracts awaiting counsel, consume none of the lane's WIP. The unit is still at an active state, since it has an open attempt. This is principle 12's split: blocked is an attempt state and does not occupy the scheduler.
- When a halt is resolved, the attempt re-enters the scheduler as a `resume` candidate under the same WIP limit.
- A `spawn` or `batch` step keeps its attempt running, so it holds lane WIP while children or the batch are outstanding, but not a slot. An Epic in progress counts against the epic WIP limit.

## Entities

### Kinds (no backend)

**`H.state(name, position[, verdict])`**. Terminal states must declare a verdict.

**`H.work`**: `.attributes`, `.fields`, `.states`, `.events`, `.timers`, `.key`.
- `.failsTo(S)` is the kind's optional failure move (principle 12). It is typed to non-active states and carried in the kind's type.

**`H.role`**: `.intents` are mapped to tools by the driver.

**`H.decision`**, **`H.memory.experience` / `.taste`** (with `.curated()`), **`H.resource`**, **`H.command`**.

**`H.flow`**: blind to kinds and states.
- Its only labels are **ends** (`.exit`, `.ends`): how the attempt finishes, in the flow's own words.
- Steps are named by key.

### Instances (adapter subpaths)

Account, model, runner, ledger and its quota partition, store, memory store, supplier, client, projection, external executable.

### Pivots

| Pivot | Composed of | Produces |
|---|---|---|
| lane | kind × suppliers × store × flow × runner × retry | where a kind's units are produced, kept and handled |
| agent | role × model or model policy × pool × playbooks | an executable that thinks |
| pool | accounts × default shares × preference × fallback | the accounts an agent may draw on |
| **playbook** | memory kind × memory store × recall policy | the plays an agent consults and that outcomes add to |
| reaction | target state × source states × attempt cancellation | a unit's answer to a received event |
| trigger | source × consequences | a recorded firing |
| threshold | metric × group × trip/reset bounds | recorded crossings |
| access | operations | what a client may do |
| harness | ledger × lanes × triggers × schedule × clients × projections | a running node (`start`) or a console (`console`) |

## Rules

### The lane maps the flow onto the kind (critique 2)

The flow never names a state. The lane's handler config is the only place where flow vocabulary meets kind vocabulary:

```
.handler(flow, {
  opens: Working,                        // active state entered when an attempt opens
  during: { draft: Drafting, approval: AwaitingApproval },  // optional: active state shown while a step runs
  ends: { sent: Sent, rejected: { to: New, upTo: 2, then: Escalated } },
  exhausted: Stalled,                    // required iff the kind has no failsTo
  params, spawns, skips,
})
```

**`during`** is keyed by the flow's own step keys (`keyof Out`, typed). It replaces the parent's `.mark`:
- the same flow can serve a kind with one active state (no `during`) and a kind with five;
- nothing is duplicated, because the flow declares no lifecycle;
- `unit.transition` records `cause: { by: 'flow', ref: step }`.

**`ends`** maps every end label to a non-active state. This is known weakness 1's "flows end at labels, the lane maps them to the kind's states". It is not a rename table: one flow serves Bug (`unfinished → Stalled`) and Feature identically, and scenario 8's experiment flow ends in `aWins` / `bWins` / `inconclusive`, which only the kind can call success or neutral.

**`Route`: `{ to, upTo, then }`** bounds a repeating end without flow arithmetic.
- The first `upTo` times this end lands for a unit, the unit goes to `to`; after that it goes to `then`.
- The count is folded from `unit.transition.end` facts on the ledger.
- This repairs scenario 2's unbounded rejection loop (`rejected: { to: New, upTo: 2, then: Escalated }`) and the contract scenario ("after the second return, Declined") with no `c.attempt.number` in the flow.

**Spawn.** A spawn step's children are made by `spawns[stepKey]`. The parent's free-string `outlet` is gone, and the key is the typed step key.

### Failure and retry (principle 12 as amended)

A failed attempt leaves the unit at its pending state, and the lane's `retry` queues the next attempt with backoff. The default is no retries.

On exhaustion the unit moves to the handler's **`exhausted`** state, which is any non-active state of the kind, typically waiting (`Stalled`). The move is recorded as `unit.transition` with `cause.by = 'retry'`.

A kind with `.failsTo(S)` moves to `S` on every failed attempt, and then `exhausted` is not accepted. This is enforced by the types: `exhausted` is required exactly when the kind's failure type is `never`.

This replaces the parked flag. Its effect is real and honest:
- a unit that is "stuck after retries" is in a state whose position is `waiting`;
- the board needs no reconciliation;
- the supervisor moves it on with `updateWork` or `sendEvents`.

### Positions

| Position | Meaning |
|---|---|
| pending | schedulable |
| active | has an open attempt (running or blocked) |
| waiting | no open attempt, not schedulable, holds nothing |
| terminal | terminal |

A Tenancy between reviews sits at `Customer` (waiting) and holds nothing.

### Outcome rate

- Rate = success / (success + failure) over units reaching terminal states, with `n` beside it.
- Neutral endings appear in `outcomes().byVerdict` and `byState`.
- `share(State)` answers "how often inconclusive".
- Success-with-warnings is a separate success state: one verdict, distinct `byState`.
- Attempt outcomes are reported separately, by `attempts()`.

### Mailbox: deferral, never silent loss (critique 3)

Every received event is recorded as `event.received`. Then, in per-unit ledger sequence order:

1. If a reaction matches the unit's current state, it applies (`event.applied`).
2. If none matches, the event is **deferred** (`event.deferred`). This is OTP `postpone`.
3. On every state change, deferred events are re-evaluated in arrival order against the new state. The first match applies.
4. If the unit becomes terminal with events still deferred, each is recorded as `event.dropped` with the terminal state.

Nothing is ignored silently, and `UnitView.deferredEvents` shows the backlog on the board.

Consequences:
- A redline or vendor reply that lands while a draft is being written is neither cancelled nor lost. When the round ends at `AwaitingCounsel` / `AwaitingVendor`, the deferred reply moves the unit to `RoundDue`.
- The next attempt's flow reads the reply through `c.events`, which is selective receive over the whole mailbox.
- Authors no longer enumerate every source state to avoid loss. `.from` lists only the states where the event should *act now*.

**Ordering.** Two events for one unit are applied in ledger sequence order. Each reaction is evaluated against the state the previous one left. A `customerReplied` that reopens a Sent conversation, followed by `ticket.solved`, closes it. That is deterministic.

**Cancellation.** A reaction from an active state must say `.cancels()`, or `start()` fails. Cancellation is always written; deferral is the default for everything else.

**Triggers on events.** `H.on.event(lane, name, { in: [States] })` filters by state entity, never by name strings. An SLA breach that arrives after `Sent` is not routed. Alternatively, trigger on the transition the reaction causes (`H.on.transition(lane, { to: [Escalated] })`).

### Typed keys, not strings

These keys are typed:
- `per` in `H.on.streak` and `H.threshold`: `keyof A`, checked against the kind's attributes;
- `during` and `spawns`: the flow's step keys;
- `ends`: the flow's end labels.

The adversary's "untyped string keys" applied only to `outlet`, which is removed. An attribute reference is a key of a typed schema, and making it an entity would add a noun with no product (principle 9).

### Timers

- A timer fires as a mailbox event `{ firedAt, deadline }`.
- An attribute timer is re-armed in the same append that changes the attribute, so an extended SLA's old deadline never fires.
- A timer with no matching reaction is deferred like any event. A recurring timer supersedes its own deferred predecessor rather than piling up.

### Fields

Store fields are loaded once when an attempt opens and are frozen for it.

### Monitors (spawn)

- Each child's terminal transition appends `monitor.down`.
- The spawn step completes when every child is down. Its output is `ChildView[]`.
- Restart reads the `monitor.down` facts. Running children are separate units and are never restarted.

### Halts, skips, budget

- Lane `skips` resolve a halt by a deterministic gate. They are recorded as `skipped` and never counted as decision samples.
- `budget.maxUsdPerUnit` is checked before every invocation. With `onExceed: 'halt'` the attempt blocks with reason `budget`, holding no WIP while it waits.

### Metrics and policies

Metrics:
- `H.metric(name).of(lane | decision | executable).hit(test)` or `.invocations(sorts)`.
- Every rate is returned as `{ rate, hits, n, window }`. Windows are a `Duration` or `'all'`.
- Queries address entities only.

Policies:
- `PolicyContext.unitOf(kind)` returns the unit typed by that kind.
- The schedule context offers `c.order(...)`, `Candidate.is(lane)` and `OpenAttempt.is(lane)`.
- Every read inside a policy is recorded in `policy.decided`.
- The kernel never starts work in a paused lane.

### Triggers and thresholds

**Sources.** `transition`, `streak`, `step`, `event` (including timers), `crossed` / `recovered`.

**Consequences.** `creates`, `sends`, `records`, `invokes`, `pauses` / `resumes`.

**Recording.**
- Each firing is recorded with its source sequence number.
- A pause and a resume are recorded as `lane.paused` / `lane.resumed` with the metric reads that caused them.

**Thresholds.**
- They hold hysteresis per group in the ledger, so one crossing means one firing.
- `trippedAt` names the episode, so an Audit keyed `category@trippedAt` is addressed exactly by its own recovery.

### Restart after a crash (scenario 10)

**Replay.** The kernel replays `step.recorded` outputs; completed steps are not run again. For the step that was running, it applies that step's restart rule:

| Rule | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `rerun` | runs the step again |
| `escalate` (the default for commands and externals) | blocks the attempt with reason `restart` |
| `ask` (the default for agents) | `Driver.settled` / `External.settled` reports whether the invocation finished |
| `{ probe }` | runs a probe command; `done: true` continues, otherwise the attempt escalates |

**State that moved while the harness was down.**
- Batches are collected through their recorded `batch.submitted`, never resubmitted.
- Halts resolved meanwhile (submitted through `console()` / `Ledger.submit`) and children that finished are ledger facts, found on restart.
- Events received meanwhile are applied in sequence order, with deferral, on restart.

**Identity and metrics.** A resumed attempt keeps its id. An interrupted invocation is excluded from every rate.

**Changed definitions.** A changed fingerprint prefix up to the running step blocks the attempt with reason `definition`. The supervisor uses `manageAttempts` to restart it from the top or abandon it.

**Single writer.** `start()` claims a fenced writer lease. A second process is refused while the lease is live, or takes over a dead holder's lease with a higher token. Stale tokens are rejected on append.

**What the author writes.** Restart rules and probes only.

### Accounts and quota (principle 15 as ruled)

- `Ledger.quota` is an append-only `QuotaPartition` of consumed, cooldown and observed events.
- Each harness appends without a lock. The kernel folds the window from all harnesses' events at every eligibility read.
- `sqlite.ledger(path, { quota: sqlite.quota(shared) })` places the partition in a shared file.
- Pool shares are defaults on the descriptor. `setShares` appends `share.set`, and the effective share is folded from those events.

### Control API

- Operations are built-ins or custom, granted through an access.
- Transport is the client adapter (MCP session, plain HTTP).
- `start()` returns `Running`; `console()` returns `Console`.

### Startup validation

`start()` fails on any of:
- duplicate names;
- an end routed to an active state;
- a `during` key that is not a step;
- a kind with active states but no `opens`;
- a reaction from an active state without `.cancels()`;
- a reaction state outside the kind;
- a flow event the kind lacks;
- an unregistered lane;
- a terminal state without a verdict;
- `restart: 'ask'` on an executable with no `settled`;
- a batch on a model that cannot batch;
- an agent without a model or pool;
- `.sets` keys that are fields;
- a `Route` with `upTo < 1`.

## Answers to the adversary

**Worst scenario 2.**
- *Approvals held WIP.* Fixed by the capacity rule: blocked attempts hold nothing.
- *Unbounded rejection loop.* Fixed by `Route` (`upTo`/`then`).
- *State-name strings in the SLA filter.* Replaced by `H.on.event(..., { in: [...] })` with state entities, or by triggering on the transition to `Escalated`.
- *Event races.* Resolved by the per-unit sequence-order rule.

**Contract counsel.**
- Counsel's verdict is a `halt` on a `Decision`, so it stays a decision metric and holds no drafting WIP.
- Returns are counted by `returned: { to: Redrafting, upTo: 2, then: Declined }`.
- A redline during drafting is deferred and applied when the round ends.

**Critique 1 (shadow statuses).** `parked` and `receiving` are deleted. Exhaustion moves to a declared state, and spawn/batch waits are a running attempt at a step. Two words remain, position and attempt status, as principle 12 defines them.

**Critique 2 (flows coupled to state names).** `.mark` is deleted. Flows name steps and ends; the lane's `during` / `ends` map them. One flow now fits kinds with any number of active states.

**Critique 3 (dropped events, string keys).** Deferral with explicit `event.dropped` replaces `event.ignored`, and nothing is lost silently. `outlet` is removed, and the remaining keys are typed.

## What changed and why

**Rename.**
- `Journal` → `Playbook` throughout: `H.playbook`, `PlaybookSpec`, `MemoryItem.playbook`.
- Reason: a journal is history and principle 14 forbids history; a playbook is forward rules with situations and reasons.

**Capacity.**
- Lane WIP is held by running attempts only. Blocked attempts release WIP, slot and account.

**Lifecycle mapping.**
- `.mark` is removed. The handler's `states` becomes `ends` plus `during` (keyed by step).
- `Route { to, upTo, then }` bounds repeating ends.
- `unit.transition` gains `end`, and `TransitionEvent` gains `end`.

**Retry exhaustion.**
- The handler gains `exhausted`, typed as required iff the kind has no `failsTo`.
- `WorkKind` and `Lane` carry the failure state as a type parameter.
- `UnitView.parked`, `unit.parked` and `unit.requeued` are removed. `Cause.by` gains `retry` and loses `supervision`.

**Mailbox.**
- `event.ignored` is replaced by `event.deferred` / `event.applied` / `event.dropped`.
- `UnitView.deferredEvents` is added.
- Per-unit sequence ordering is stated.

**Spawn.** `outlet` is removed; `spawns` is keyed by the spawn step key.

**Triggers.** `H.on.event` gains a state-entity filter `{ in }`.

**Removed.** `ReceiveView`, `AttemptView.receiving`, the `mark` step sort.

**Adapters.** They take `KindRef<A, F, St, Ev>`, the kind's data shape, instead of the full `WorkKind` generic list, so adding the failure parameter did not widen every adapter signature.

## Principles broken

none.

import { H } from 'harness-dsl';
import { z } from 'zod';
import * as sqlite from 'harness-dsl/sqlite';

const Queued = H.state('Queued', 'pending');
const Building = H.state('Building', 'active');
const Stalled = H.state('Stalled', 'waiting');
const Done = H.state('Done', 'terminal', 'success');
const Abandoned = H.state('Abandoned', 'terminal', 'failure');
const ticketStates = [Queued, Building, Stalled, Done, Abandoned];

const Proposed = H.state('Proposed', 'pending');
const Planning = H.state('Planning', 'active');
const Underway = H.state('Underway', 'active');
const Delivered = H.state('Delivered', 'terminal', 'success');

const Due = H.state('Due', 'pending');
const Probing = H.state('Probing', 'active');
const Healthy = H.state('Healthy', 'terminal', 'success');
const Unhealthy = H.state('Unhealthy', 'terminal', 'failure');

const ticketAttributes = { ref: z.string(), title: z.string(), area: z.string() };
const ticketFields = { description: z.string() };

const Bug = H.work('bug')
  .attributes(ticketAttributes)
  .fields(ticketFields)
  .states(ticketStates)
  .key(u => u.attributes.ref);

const Feature = H.work('feature')
  .attributes(ticketAttributes)
  .fields(ticketFields)
  .states(ticketStates)
  .key(u => u.attributes.ref);

const Epic = H.work('epic')
  .attributes({ ref: z.string(), title: z.string() })
  .fields({ description: z.string() })
  .states([Proposed, Planning, Underway, Stalled, Delivered, Abandoned])
  .key(u => u.attributes.ref);

const Heartbeat = H.work('service-heartbeat')
  .attributes({ service: z.string(), at: z.number() })
  .states([Due, Probing, Healthy, Unhealthy])
  .failsTo(Unhealthy)
  .key(u => `${u.attributes.service}@${u.attributes.at}`);

const subscriptionA = claudeCode.subscription('claude-max-a', { configDir: H.env('CLAUDE_CONFIG_A') });
const subscriptionB = claudeCode.subscription('claude-max-b', { configDir: H.env('CLAUDE_CONFIG_B') });
const subscriptionC = claudeCode.subscription('claude-max-c', { configDir: H.env('CLAUDE_CONFIG_C') });
const apiAccount = anthropic.account('anthropic-api', { apiKey: H.env('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY') });

const soonestExpiring = H.policy.account('soonest-expiring-first', c =>
  c.eligible.slice().sort((a, b) => a.windowEndsAt - b.windowEndsAt)[0] ?? null);

const claudePool = H.pool('claude-subscriptions')
  .accounts([
    { account: subscriptionA, share: 0.5 },
    { account: subscriptionB, share: 0.3 },
    { account: subscriptionC, share: 0.2 },
  ])
  .prefer(soonestExpiring)
  .fallback(apiAccount);

const sonnet = claudeCode.model('claude-sonnet-4-5');
const opus = claudeCode.model('claude-opus-4-1');

const builderModel = H.policy.model('builder-cheap-until-it-slips', [sonnet, opus], c => {
  const cheap = c.metrics.success({ kind: c.unit?.kind, model: sonnet, window: { days: 14 } });
  if (cheap.n < 20) return sonnet;
  return cheap.rate !== null && cheap.rate < 0.85 ? opus : sonnet;
});

const trackRate = (x: { track: { present: number; succeeded: number } }) =>
  (x.track.succeeded + 1) / (x.track.present + 2);

const specificThenProven = H.policy.recall('specific-then-proven', c =>
  c.candidates
    .slice()
    .sort((a, b) => b.specificity - a.specificity || trackRate(b) - trackRate(a))
    .slice(0, c.limit));

const experience = H.playbook('coding-experience', H.memory.experience('coding-experience').curated())
  .store(jsonl.memory('.harness/memory/experience.jsonl'))
  .recall(specificThenProven);

const taste = H.playbook('owner-taste', H.memory.taste('owner-taste'))
  .store(jsonl.memory('.harness/memory/taste.jsonl'))
  .recall(specificThenProven);

  .instructions('Implement the task in the worktree. Address every listed deficit. Ask the owner when a decision is theirs.')
  .input({ task: z.string(), deficits: z.array(z.string()) })
  .output({ summary: z.string() });

const auditorRole = H.role('auditor')
  .intents(['read', 'execute', 'remember'])

  .output({ features: z.array(z.object({ title: z.string(), description: z.string() })) });

const builder = H.agent('builder', builderRole)
  .model(builderModel)
  .pool(claudePool)
  .recalls([experience, taste])

const auditor = H.agent('auditor', auditorRole)
  .model(sonnet)
  .pool(claudePool)

const ticketFlow = H.flow('build-and-audit')

      .step('build', builder, c => ({
        task: `${c.input.title}\n\n${c.input.description}`,

      }))
      .step('audit', auditor, c => ({
        task: `${c.input.title}\n\n${c.input.description}`,
        summary: c.out.build.summary,

    last => last.audit.deficits.length === 0 ? null : { deficits: last.audit.deficits },
  )
  .ends(['done', 'unfinished'], c => c.out.rounds.exhausted ? 'unfinished' : 'done');

const epicFlow = H.flow('decompose-epic')

const Handling = H.state('Handling', 'active');

const opus = anthropic.model('claude-opus-4-1');

  reply: z.string(),
  note: z.string(),
});

const trackRate = (x: { track: { present: number; succeeded: number } }) =>
  (x.track.succeeded + 1) / (x.track.present + 2);

const specificThenProven = H.policy.recall('specific-then-proven', c =>

  .output({ reply: z.string() });

const drafterModel = H.policy.model('drafter-by-approval', [sonnet, opus], (c, options) => {
  const unit = c.unitOf(Conversation);
  const reads = options.map(model => ({
    model,
    rate: c.metrics.read(approvalRate, {
      kind: Conversation,
      model,
      where: unit ? { category: unit.attributes.category } : undefined,
      window: { days: 30 },
    }),
  }));
  const thin = reads.filter(r => r.rate.n < 30)[0];
  if (thin) return thin.model;
  return reads.reduce((best, r) => (r.rate.rate ?? 0) > (best.rate.rate ?? 0) ? r : best).model;
});

const classifier = H.agent('classifier', classifierRole).model(haiku).pool(apiAccount);

const drafter = H.agent('drafter', drafterRole)
  .model(drafterModel)

    subject: c.input.subject,
    message: c.events.customerReplied[c.events.customerReplied.length - 1]?.payload.text ?? c.input.message,
  }))
  .sets({ category: z.string() }, c => ({ category: c.out.classify.category }))
  .step('draft', drafter, c => ({
    subject: c.input.subject,

  })

        },
        decision: { verdict: 'approve', reply: '', note: 'skipped: category proven safe' },

const Queued = H.state('Queued', 'pending');

const Parked = H.state('Parked', 'terminal', 'neutral');
